Excellent! I can see the issue clearly. Both pods are crashing with the same error. The logs show that the pricing-engine is failing when compiling a rule called "BF-2026-STACKED" with an index out of range panic. The error occurs in the TierTable.Lookup function when trying to access index 3 of a 3-element array (which should only have indices 0-2).

The key detail is that the application fetched 1,204 active rules from rules-admin (revision 8841), and one of those rules (BF-2026-STACKED) has invalid data - it declares 3 tiers but the code is trying to access the 4th tier (index 3).

This is not a Kubernetes issue - it's a data issue. The pricing rules data has become corrupted or invalid. Since the ticket states that no deployment has happened since April and nobody touched the cluster today, this suggests that the pricing rules have been updated externally (likely through the pricing-rules-admin service), and a new rule or updated rule has been added with incorrect configuration.

Let me update the ticket with this finding:

input.note:
The pricing-engine pods are crashing due to invalid pricing rules data, not a Kubernetes issue. Both pods show the same panic error: "index out of range [3] with length 3" when compiling rule BF-2026-STACKED. The logs show the application is fetching 1,204 active rules from rules-admin (revision 8841) and crashes during compilation of a rule that declares 3 tiers but attempts to access a 4th tier.

Evidence: Both pricing-engine pods crashed at ~2pm with exit code 2, showing identical stack traces in their logs. The error originates from internal/rules/tiers.go:88 during TierTable.Lookup, indicating corrupted or misconfigured rule data.

Fix: Review the pricing rules in rules-admin, specifically rule BF-2026-STACKED. Check its tier configuration and correct the mismatch between the declared tier count (3) and the tier indices being accessed in the rule logic. Once the invalid rule is fixed or removed from the active rules, the pods should recover automatically as Kubernetes will restart them and they'll load the corrected rules.
